newsitem.title: BELGIUM: DEMAND FOR NEW 10-YR SEEN SUPPORTING BELGIAN OLOS.
newsitem.headline: DEMAND FOR NEW 10-YR SEEN SUPPORTING BELGIAN OLOS.

text.p: Demand for the new 10-year benchmark OLO at Monday's regular Treasury auction was seen supporting the overall Belgian linear bond market despite Friday's weakness, dealers said.
"I think people will be very aggressive in the auction, just to get the new benchmark. I think a lot of people are short...I don't think the spread will go wider," one trader said.

The benchmark March 2007 yield ended at 5.84 percent on Friday, up from 5.78 on Thursday, as stronger-than-expected German inflation and import price data pushed Bunds lower. The spread edged out one basis point to seven.

During the session the German states of Bavaria, Baden-Wuerttemberg and North Rhine Westphalia reported annual inflation rates of 1.6, 1.7 and 2.0 percent, disappointing the market. Bundesbank Vice President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum also said rates would remain on hold in the coming weeks.
The German data pushed money rates back over 3.00 percent and OLO dealers said the growing fear the German rate easing cycle may be over flattened the OLO curve.
One trader said, however, the shape of the five to 10-year area remained little changed.
At Monday's auction the Treasury is also selling the 5.00 pct OLO, maturing 2001.
European Union finance ministers are also due to hold a regular meeting in Brussels.
